requirements.heading: Submission Identification
requirements.text: A site MAY choose to use port 25 for message submission by designating some hosts to be MSAs and others to be MTAs.

requirements.heading: Message Rejection and Bouncing
requirements.text: MTAs and MSAs MAY implement message rejection rules that rely, in part, on whether the message is a submission or a relay.

requirements.heading: Message Rejection and Bouncing
requirements.text: If an MSA is not able to determine a return path to the submitting user, from a valid MAIL FROM, a valid source IP address, or based on authenticated identity, then the MSA SHOULD immediately reject the message.

requirements.heading: Message Rejection and Bouncing
requirements.text: Note that a null return path, that is, MAIL FROM:<>, is permitted and MUST NOT, in itself, be cause for rejecting a message.

requirements.heading: Message Rejection and Bouncing
requirements.text: Except in the case where the MSA is unable to determine a valid return path for the message being submitted, text in this specification that instructs an MSA to issue a rejection code MAY be complied with by accepting the message and subsequently generating a bounce message.

requirements.heading: Mandatory Actions
requirements.text: An MSA MUST do all of the following:

requirements.heading: Ensure All Domains Are Fully Qualified
requirements.text: The MSA MUST ensure that all domains in the SMTP envelope are fully qualified.

requirements.heading: Ensure All Domains Are Fully Qualified
requirements.text: If the MSA examines or alters the message text in any way, except to add trace header fields [SMTP-MTA], it MUST ensure that all domains in address header fields are fully qualified.

requirements.heading: Ensure All Domains Are Fully Qualified
requirements.text: Local conventions that permit single-level domains SHOULD reject, rather than expand, incomplete multi-level domains (e.g., 'squeaky.sales'), since such expansion is particularly risky.

requirements.heading: Require Authentication
requirements.text: The MSA MUST, by default, issue an error response to the MAIL command if the session has not been authenticated using [SMTP-AUTH], unless it has already independently established authentication or authorization (such as being within a protected subnetwork).

requirements.heading: Recommended Actions
requirements.text: The MSA SHOULD do all of the following.

requirements.heading: Enforce Address Syntax
requirements.text: An MSA SHOULD reject messages with illegal syntax in a sender or recipient SMTP envelope address.

requirements.heading: Enforce Address Syntax
requirements.text: If the MSA examines or alters the message text in any way, except to add trace header fields, it SHOULD reject messages with illegal address syntax in address header fields.

requirements.heading: Log Errors
requirements.text: The MSA SHOULD log message errors, especially apparent misconfigurations of client software.

requirements.heading: Apply Shorter Timeouts
requirements.text: Submission servers SHOULD respond to any command (even DATA) in fewer than 2 minutes.

requirements.heading: Apply Shorter Timeouts
requirements.text: When the submission server has a close administrative and/or network relationship with the submission client(s) -- e.g., with a webmail interface calling on a tightly bound submission server -- mutual agreement on much shorter timeouts MAY be appropriate.

requirements.heading: Optional Actions
requirements.text: The MSA MAY do any of the following.

requirements.heading: Enforce Submission Rights
requirements.text: The MSA MAY issue an error response to a MAIL command if the address in MAIL FROM appears to have insufficient submission rights or is not authorized with the authentication used (if the session has been authenticated).

requirements.heading: Enforce Permissions
requirements.text: The MSA MAY issue an error response to a RCPT command if inconsistent with the permissions given to the user (if the session has been authenticated).

requirements.heading: Check Message Data
requirements.text: The MSA MAY issue an error response to the DATA command or send a failure result after end-of-data if the submitted message is syntactically invalid, seems inconsistent with permissions given to the user (if known), or violates site policy in some way.

requirements.heading: Support for the Postmaster Address
requirements.text: If appropriate under local conditions and to facilitate conformance with the "postmaster" requirements of [SMTP-MTA], the MSA MAY permit a reduced degree of authentication for mail addressed to the "postmaster" (or one of its alternate spelling forms, see

requirements.heading: Adjust Character Encodings
requirements.text: Subject to limits imposed by other protocols and specifications, the MSA MAY convert among character sets or string encodings to improve message usefulness, likelihood of delivery, or conformance with other specifications or recommendations.

requirements.heading: Adjust Character Encodings
requirements.text: Such conversions MAY include, when necessary, replacement of addresses whose encoding does not conform to RFC 5321 with ones that do, using information available out of band.

requirements.heading: Interaction with SMTP Extensions
requirements.text: +--------------------+----------------------+--------+-----------------+ | Keyword | Name |Sub- | Reference | | | |mission | | +--------------------+----------------------+--------+-----------------+ |PIPELINING |Pipelining |SHOULD |[PIPELINING] | |ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES |Enhanced Status Codes |SHOULD |[CODES-EXTENSION]| |ETRN |Extended Turn |MUST NOT|[ETRN] | | ...

requirements.heading: Interaction with SMTP Extensions
requirements.text: |Extended Codes |SHOULD |[SMTP-CODES] | |DSN |Delivery Status |SHOULD |[DSN] | | | Notification | | | |SIZE |Message size |MAY |[SIZE] | | ...

requirements.heading: Interaction with SMTP Extensions
requirements.text: Future SMTP extensions SHOULD explicitly specify if they are valid on the Submission port.

requirements.heading: Interaction with SMTP Extensions
requirements.text: Extended Status Codes [SMTP-CODES] SHOULD be supported and used according to [CODES-EXTENSION].

requirements.heading: Interaction with SMTP Extensions
requirements.text: [PIPELINING] SHOULD be supported by the MSA.

requirements.heading: Interaction with SMTP Extensions
requirements.text: [SMTP-AUTH] allows the MSA to validate the authority and determine the identity of the submitting user and MUST be supported by the MSA.

requirements.heading: Message Modifications
requirements.text: Sites MAY modify submissions to ensure compliance with standards and site policy.

requirements.heading: Message Modifications
requirements.text: Any message forwarded or delivered by the MSA MUST conform to the requirements of [SMTP-MTA] and [MESSAGE-FORMAT] or the requirements permitted by extensions that are supported by the MSA and accepted by the next-hop server.

requirements.heading: Add 'Sender'
requirements.text: The MSA MAY add or replace the 'Sender' field, if the identity of the sender is known and this is not given in the 'From' field.

requirements.heading: Add 'Sender'
requirements.text: The MSA MUST ensure that any address it places in a 'Sender' field is, in fact, a valid mail address.

requirements.heading: Add 'Date'
requirements.text: The MSA MAY add a 'Date' field to the submitted message, if it lacks it, or correct the 'Date' field if it does not conform to [MESSAGE-FORMAT] syntax.

requirements.heading: Add 'Message-ID'
requirements.text: The MSA SHOULD add or replace the 'Message-ID' field, if it lacks it, or it is not valid syntax (as defined by [MESSAGE-FORMAT]).

requirements.heading: Transfer Encode
requirements.text: The MSA MAY apply transfer encoding to the message according to MIME conventions, if needed and not harmful to the MIME type.

requirements.heading: Sign the Message
requirements.text: The MSA MAY (digitally) sign or otherwise add authentication information to the message.

requirements.heading: Encrypt the Message
requirements.text: The MSA MAY encrypt the message for transport to reflect organizational policies.

requirements.heading: Resolve Aliases
requirements.text: The MSA MAY resolve and rewrite aliases (e.g., Canonical Name (CNAME) records) for domain names, in the SMTP envelope and/or in address fields of the header, subject to local policy.

requirements.heading: Header Rewriting
requirements.text: The MSA MAY rewrite local parts and/or domains in the SMTP envelope and, optionally, in address fields of the header, according to local policy.

requirements.heading: Header Rewriting
requirements.text: The MSA MUST NOT rewrite a forward-pointing (destination) address in a way that violates the constraints of [SMTP-MTA] on modifications of local-parts.

requirements.heading: Informative References
requirements.text: As part of this, reclassified RFC 4954 to a normative reference (SMTP AUTH is a MUST for RFC 4409 and this specification).
